meaning: Background operation is an execution mode, not a different analytic scenario; sources and current prototypes must be separated.
Scenario, execution plan, Case, Job, Attempt, Automation and ChatThread differ in lifetime/identity; current status names overlap.
Node/host, automation and job have separate lifecycles; headless execution proposed beyond Qt worker/GUI process.
A background job belongs to user analytical context but need not create a separate chat; ChatThread is a new target entity.
Universal launch can choose foreground/background/schedule but must check current chat scope, permissions and compatibility.
Dynamic active-chat group should be derived from jobs without permanently mutating user order; archived chat must not delete job.
Task/automation center offers cross-chat overview while chat retains context; two projections, one execution authority.
Automation definition and trigger/schedule occurrence are not running Job and have independent owner, enabled and policy states.
Timezone/DST/nonexistent times, misfire, catch-up budget and dependency/condition triggers need explicit semantics.
Lifecycle, terminal disposition and attention/health are orthogonal; single status cannot show outcome truth.
Queue cancellation, cooperative execution cancellation and irreversible effect handling differ; progress percent needs known denominator.
Resource conflict, fairness, concurrency policy, lease and fencing matter independently of chat count.
Transactional node truth, recovery and reconnect snapshot/event cursors are candidate; SQLite WAL is a conditional local implementation.
Shared/node automations and jobs require scoped grants and no hidden interactive prompt in unattended worker.
Product job status and external node/problem observations are distinct; shared notices require audience/ACL filtering.
Illustrative typed execution, automation and command APIs include stable identities and transactional idempotent submit; no accepted API fields or URI.
Proposed host service/worker and scheduler adapters are alternative realizations; scheduler library alone does not own Product job truth.
UI, engine, security and fault-injection acceptance matrices are proposed negative cases, not executed test results.
Nine candidate migration slices and explicit non-goals reject separate background-only and cognitive-only engines.
Chat creation, rule journal, pinning, scheduling calendar, concurrency and node profile remain product choices.
Study synthesizes earlier Windows/observability/other research and technical references, not independent empirical confirmation.
